newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition ready to consider new leader.
newsitem.headline: India coalition ready to consider new leader.

text.p: India's defeated coalition is willing to consider a replacement for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in efforts to make a new political deal with the Congress party, a close aide of a senior negotiator said on Saturday.

"There is no other way," the aide, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters as the decision-making Steering Committee of the centre-left United Front held a meeting following Deve Gowda's defeat in a confidence vote on Friday.

The coalition's ally-turned-foe Congress party withdrew vital support to the coalition on March 30 and has refused to resume backing unless the alliance changes its leader. The United Front had repeatedly refused to yield ground so far.

The front was still weighing its options but was now considering a leadership change, the aide said. He added that Deve Gowda, still considered the senior leader of the 15-party United Front, was keen to face elections.
"Deve Gowda says they (the alliance) can do well in an election. But there are others in the United Front who do not want a mid-term poll," the aide said.

The 10-month-old government was formed last June by the alliance, which has 178 lawmakers, with support from the Congress party, which has 140 deputies in the 545-member lower house. They closed ranks last year to keep out the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), with its 193 deputies.
